description: Apparatus #1: a constrained dialogic drafting assignment where drafting support is gated behind dialogic contribution. Investigates threshold-calibration and the evidential value of the AI chat transcript for student engagement.

Instrument view of a Canvas research apparatus: what dialogic contribution means as a measured quantity, what process signals conceptually record, the threshold as a research variable, and how evidence cites apparatus identity and configuration.
CAMDLE as a proposed learning design: a generative writing assistant whose drafting support is conditional on prior dialogic contribution — a research agenda, not an efficacy claim.
Observation → documented experience → structured experiment → replication/challenge → synthesis → finding: the contribution model that lets ordinary teachers contribute without writing papers.

Tiered claim governance: low-friction entry (auto-approval at provisional/tentative via deterministic rules), high-bar promotion (supported requires human review), challenge-anything, direction-of-fit pre-registration.
Central research question: how the drafting-unlock threshold should vary by task type, proficiency level, language background, and learner strategy.
